mainTopic: Two versions of the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about a שכיב מרע's spoken instructions (Shabbat vs. weekday) and about acquiring for a גדול vs. a קטן; then a new משנה about a house that collapsed on a son and his father, where nobody knows who died first.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא with two versions of a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The first is about whether a שכיב מרע's spoken instructions count on a weekday or on Shabbat. The second is about whether one may acquire property for an adult or a minor. In each version רבי אליעזר limits the rule to one case, and רבי יהושע uses a קל וחומר to include the other; רבי יהודה reports both disputes the opposite way. Then a new משנה begins: a house fell on a son and his father, and the son owed a כתובה and a debt. בית שמאי say the father's heirs and the son's creditors split the property. בית הלל say the property stays with its last known owner, the father's heirs. The גמרא brings שמואל's question about דאיקני: does a lien on property the borrower acquires later reach that property once he sells it or it passes to his heirs? רב יוסף's proof is rejected by רבא. רב חנא then tries to prove it from our משנה, and רב נחמן answers that the creditors collect only because orphans have a מצוה to pay their father's debts. רב אשי objects that such a debt would be like an oral loan, which cannot be collected from heirs.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: weekday rule applies all the more so on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: In the first version of the ברייתא, רבי יהושע says a שכיב מרע's spoken instructions are valid on a weekday, so they are surely valid on Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The חכמים taught this rule about a weekday, and all the more so it applies on Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a ברייתא in the middle. רבי יהושע is answering רבי אליעזר, who in this first version had said a dying man's spoken words count only on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי אליעזר had limited the rule to a weekday and excluded Shabbat. רבי יהושע argues that the rule was taught for a weekday, when writing is possible. So it surely holds on Shabbat, when writing is forbidden. This is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill (on his deathbed).
On a weekday.
A 'how much more so' argument, reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one.
'They said', meaning the חכמים taught this rule.

phrases.english: says: With regard to a weekday they said it,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהושע, named right before this, answering רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: and all the more so it applies to Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first version of the ברייתא, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, a שכיב מרע's spoken instructions are valid on weekdays, and all the more so on Shabbat.

steps.title: Acquiring on behalf of an adult or a minor, first version
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says one can acquire for an adult but not for a minor. רבי יהושע says the rule was taught for an adult, so it surely applies to a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, one may acquire property on behalf of an adult, but not on behalf of a minor. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: They taught it about an adult, and all the more so it applies to a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists a second מחלוקת that follows the same pattern. This one is about acquiring something for another person without his involvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר limits זכייה to an adult, who could acquire for himself. רבי יהושע turns this into a קל וחומר. If one may acquire for an adult, who could do it himself, then surely one may acquire for a minor, who cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly; a case that follows the same pattern.
One may acquire (something) on behalf of another person.
An adult.
A minor.

phrases.english: Similarly,
one may acquire on behalf of an adult,
but one may not acquire on behalf of a minor;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They said it about an adult,
all the more so for a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ – זָכִין לַגָּדוֹל, וְאֵין זָכִין לַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel מחלוקת, built the same way as step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבי אליעזר allows זכייה only for an adult. רבי יהושע extends it to a minor through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבי אליעזר takes the narrow view (only a weekday; only a גדול). רבי יהושע uses a קל וחומר each time to include the other case too.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: Shabbat versus weekday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that רבי אליעזר validates spoken instructions only on Shabbat, since he can't write. רבי יהושע says the rule was taught for Shabbat, so it surely applies on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says that רבי אליעזר says: On Shabbat the sick man's words stand, because he cannot write, but not on a weekday. רבי יהושע says: They taught it about Shabbat, and all the more so it applies on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא, רבי יהודה, gives his own report of how the מחלוקת went. In his version, the קל וחומר runs in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's report, רבי אליעזר gives a reason: on Shabbat writing is impossible, so spoken words must count, but not on a weekday. רבי יהושע argues the other way. If the חכמים trusted his words on Shabbat, they surely did on a weekday. Both versions agree that רבי יהושע validates both days; only the wording of his argument is flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand, meaning his spoken instructions are legally valid.
Because he is unable to write.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. Here the קל וחומר goes from Shabbat to weekday, the opposite of step 1, but רבי יהושע's bottom line is the same: the words count on both days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says that Rabbi Eliezer says:
On Shabbat, his words stand,
phrases.notes: 'His words' means the spoken instructions of the dangerously ill man.

phrases.english: because he is unable to write;
but not on a weekday.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They said it about Shabbat,
all the more so on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, reversed report of the same מחלוקת from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר validates spoken instructions only on Shabbat. רבי יהושע validates them on weekdays too, through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: acquiring for a minor or an adult
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר allows acquiring for a minor but not for an adult. רבי יהושע says the rule was taught for a minor, so it surely applies to an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, one may acquire on behalf of a minor but not on behalf of an adult. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: They taught it about a minor, and all the more so it applies to an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה's version continues with the parallel זכייה case. This one is also reversed from the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אליעזר limits זכייה to a קטן, who cannot acquire for himself. He does not allow it for a גדול, who can do it himself. רבי יהושע reasons with a קל וחומר: if one may acquire for a minor, surely one may for an adult. So in both versions רבי יהושע allows זכייה for both.

keyTerms.meaning: One may acquire on behalf of a minor.
One may not acquire on behalf of an adult.

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions swap which case רבי אליעזר limits the rule to. In both, רבי יהושע uses a קל וחומר to include both cases.

phrases.english: Similarly,
one may acquire on behalf of a minor, but one may not acquire on behalf of an adult,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They said it about a minor,
all the more so for an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ – זָכִין לַקָּטָן וְאֵין זָכִין לַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהודה's reversed version with the matching זכייה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, רבי אליעזר allows זכייה only for a minor. רבי יהושע extends it to an adult through a קל וחומר.

steps.title: New משנה: a house falls on a son and his father
steps.stepSummary: A house collapses on a son and his father, and no one knows who died first. The son owed a כתובה and a debt. The father's heirs say the son died first; the creditors say the father died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A house fell on a man and his father, or on a man and someone he would inherit from. The man owed his wife's כתובה and owed money to a creditor. The father's heirs say: The son died first, and then the father died. The creditors say: The father died first, and then the son died.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lays out the case. This step sets up the dispute; the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each order of death leads to a different result. If the father died first, the son inherited his property for a moment, so the son's wife and creditors can collect from it. If the son died first, he never inherited, and everything goes to the father's other heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה.
People he would inherit from.
The money a husband owes his wife under her marriage contract.
A creditor.
The father's heirs.

steps.confusionAlert: Each side's claim matches its own interest. The creditors need the father to have died first so the son inherited before he died. The heirs need the son to have died first.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A house fell on him and on his father,
or on him and on those he inherits from,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב,
phrases.english: and he owed a wife's כתובה and a creditor,
the father's heirs say:

phrases.aramaic: הַבֵּן מֵת רִאשׁוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הָאָב;
phrases.english: The son died first, and afterward the father died;
and the creditors say:

phrases.aramaic: הָאָב מֵת רִאשׁוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הַבֵּן.
phrases.english: The father died first, and afterward the son died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: an inheritance where the order of death is unknown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the order of death is unknown, and the heirs and creditors each make the claim that helps them.

steps.title: בית שמאי: split it; בית הלל: property stays where it was
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי rule that the heirs and creditors divide the property. בית הלל rule that the property stays in its existing ownership, so it goes to the father's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: They divide the property. בית הלל say: The property stays in its previous ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ruling on the case from step 5. There are two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי split the property because neither side can prove its claim. בית הלל follow the property's last known status. The property last belonged to the father, so it goes to his heirs, and the creditors would need proof to take it.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide (the property) between them.
The property stays in its existing ownership status.
A presumed or established status that stays until proven otherwise.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's rule, נכסים בחזקתן: when we can't tell who died first, the property stays in its known previous ownership, so the father's heirs keep it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic case of ruling when the facts can't be known. It shows the two approaches: split the doubtful property, or leave it with its last known owner.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: They divide,
and Beit Hillel say: The property stays in its prior status.
phrases.notes: The last known owner was the father, so his heirs keep it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the heirs and creditors divide the property. בית הלל: the property stays in its prior status, with the father's heirs.

steps.title: Background rule: a loan with a document versus a loan with only witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere. A loan written in a שטר can be collected from sold property. A loan made only before witnesses can be collected only from unsold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: someone who lends money with a written document can collect even from property that has since been sold. If he lent only in front of witnesses, he can collect only from property the borrower still owns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a basic rule about collecting loans. This sets up שמואל's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A written שטר is public, so buyers are expected to know about the debt. That is why the lender may take back property they bought from the borrower. A loan made only before witnesses is less public, so the lender can collect only from what the borrower still owns.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, meaning in a משנה in another place
A written document, here a loan document
Liened property: property the borrower has sold, which is still tied to the debt
Free property: property the borrower still owns

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in another place, later in this מסכתא.

phrases.english: One who lends to his fellow with a document
collects from liened properties.
With witnesses only
he collects from free properties.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא on the collapsed-house משנה opens with a background rule about liens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan with a שטר can be collected from sold property. A loan made only before witnesses can be collected only from unsold property.

steps.title: שמואל asks about a lien on property the borrower will acquire later
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks: if the borrower wrote "whatever I will acquire is liened," and he later acquired property, does the lien take effect?
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל asked: if the borrower wrote "property that I will acquire" is liened to this loan, and he then acquired property, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל asks whether a lien can take hold of property the borrower did not yet own when the loan was written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 7 covers property the borrower owned when he took the loan. Here the borrower tried to lien future property in advance. The question is whether that clause works once he actually buys something.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks, raises a question he is unsure about
"That I will acquire": a clause liening future property to the loan

phrases.english: Shmuel asks:
"That I will acquire," and he acquired; what is the law?
phrases.notes: The borrower wrote in the loan document that anything he buys later is tied to the loan, and then he bought some property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lien rule of step 7 and asks about property acquired after the loan.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a דאיקני clause create a lien on property the borrower acquires later?

steps.title: The question only arises according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, a person can transfer something not yet in existence, so the lien certainly works. The question is asked only according to the רבנן, who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world, there is no question: the lender certainly gets the lien. The question is according to the רבנן, who say a person cannot transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows שמואל's question. It explains which opinion the question really depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liening property you do not yet own is like transferring something that does not exist yet. For רבי מאיר that is fine, so there is nothing to ask. For the רבנן it normally does not work, so we wonder whether a lien is different.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Something that has not yet come into the world, meaning it does not yet exist or is not yet his
Don't ask it, because the answer is obvious
Transfers ownership or rights

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, who says:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם –
phrases.english: A person can transfer something that has not come into the world
you should not ask, for he certainly acquired.
phrases.notes: "He" is the lender: his lien certainly takes hold.

phrases.english: Rather, when should you ask?
According to the Rabbis, who say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: A person cannot transfer something that has not come into the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact scope of שמואל's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion is the question based on? It is asked according to the רבנן, for whom a lien on future property might not work.

steps.title: רב יוסף tries to prove the lien from the clever lender case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings the חכמים's ruling that a lender who sold land to his borrower was being smart, because he can now collect that land for his loan. This suggests property the borrower acquires later is liened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear a proof. The חכמים say: this lender was clever to sell him the land, because now he can take it as collateral for the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer שמואל's question with a proof from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the borrower bought the field after the loan. Still, the חכמים say the lender can collect it for the debt. רב יוסף concludes that property acquired after the loan becomes liened.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
Clever, smart
To take it as collateral, to seize it for the debt

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
And the Rabbis say:
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in כתובות 110a. The borrower showed that the lender later sold him a field.

phrases.english: This one was clever
in that he sold him the land,
because he can take it as collateral from him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to answer the question.
steps.raayaObject: That property acquired after the loan is liened to the debt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים in the משנה in כתובות: the lender can collect the field he sold to the borrower after the loan.

steps.title: רבא: collecting from the borrower himself proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. A lender can collect from anything the borrower holds right now, even the cloak on his back. That has nothing to do with a lien.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Are you talking about collecting from the borrower himself? From him, the lender can collect even from the cloak on his shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the clever lender case, the field is still in the borrower's hands. Anything a borrower currently owns can be collected, whenever he got it. So the case says nothing about a lien that would follow the property after it leaves him.

keyTerms.meaning: From him, meaning from the borrower himself
Cloak
His shoulder

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse collecting from the borrower with having a lien. A lien matters only once the property has moved to someone else, like a buyer or an heir.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Is he speaking about collecting from him?!
From him, even from the cloak that is on his shoulders!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the clever lender case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is about collecting from the borrower himself, which is always allowed. It is not about a lien on property that has left his hands.

steps.title: The real question: he acquired, then sold or left it to heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבא restates the question. The real issue is a borrower who acquired property and then sold it, or left it to his heirs. Can the lender take it from them?
steps.simpleTranslation: What we were really asking about is "that I will acquire" where he acquired and then sold, or "that I will acquire" where he acquired and then left it to his heirs. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sharpens שמואל's question to show what is really being asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lien only matters once the property leaves the borrower's hands. So the question is whether the דאיקני clause lets the lender take the property back from a buyer or an heir. This ties back to step 7's rule about sold property, and to the heirs in the collapsed-house משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What we were asking about
He sold
He left it to his heirs

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's question about דאיקני is whether a lien on future property follows it after it is sold or inherited. Collecting from the borrower himself is never in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the סוגיא. It connects to the משנה's dispute between the father's heirs and the son's creditors.

phrases.english: When it was a question for us,
"That I will acquire," and he acquired and sold;
"That I will acquire," and he acquired and left it to heirs; what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof, רבא restates the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a lender with a דאיקני clause take the later-acquired property from a buyer or from the borrower's heirs?

steps.title: רב חנא quotes the משנה of the collapsed house
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא cites a משנה: a house falls on a son and his father. The son owed a כתובה and a creditor. The father's heirs say the son died first, and the creditors say the father died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא said: Come and hear. A house fell on a man and his father, or on a man and someone he would inherit from. The man owed his wife's כתובה and a creditor. The father's heirs say the son died first and then the father. The creditors say the father died first, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא begins a proof by quoting a משנה about a son and father who died together. This step sets up the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of deaths decides who gets the father's estate. If the father died first, the son inherited it for a moment before he died, and then his creditors want to collect from it. The son only got this property after he borrowed, so it is a real-life case of property acquired later.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula that introduces a proof from a source
those he would inherit from
a wife's marriage contract payment
a creditor
the father's other heirs

phrases.english: Rav Chana said: Come and hear:
The house fell on him and on his father,
on him and on those he inherits from;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב;
phrases.english: and he owed a wife's כתובה and a creditor;
the father's heirs say:

phrases.aramaic: הַבֵּן מֵת רִאשׁוֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הָאָב,
phrases.english: The son died first and afterward the father died,
and the creditors say:
The father died first, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer רבא's question from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That property acquired after the loan and passed to heirs is liened.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the house that fell on a son and his father.

steps.title: Why the משנה shows later-acquired property is liened
steps.stepSummary: If דאיקני property that was then inherited were not liened, the creditors would gain nothing by proving the father died first. The משנה treats their claim as meaningful, so the lien must work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that when a borrower writes 'what I will acquire' and then acquires and sells, or acquires and leaves it to his heirs, it is not liened, then there is a problem. Even if the father did die first, this is still 'what I will acquire'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves the point. The creditors' argument only makes sense if property the son got after the loan is liened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the father died first, the son got his father's property after he borrowed, and it then passed to his own heirs. That is exactly 'acquired and then left to heirs.' Since the משנה takes the creditors' claim seriously, such property must be liened.

he acquired and left it to his heirs
is liened (pledged to the lender)

phrases.english: And if you think that with "what I will acquire," if he acquired and sold,
or with "what I will acquire," if he acquired and left it to heirs,
it is not liened;
then even granting that the father died first,

phrases.notes: The son received the property only after he borrowed, so it counts as later-acquired property that he left to his heirs.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. The 'father's heirs' are the other heirs of the father who died in the collapse. The son's creditors are trying to collect from what the son himself would have inherited from that father.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: A דאיקני lien reaches property that was acquired later and then inherited.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The creditors' claim in the משנה would be pointless unless such property were liened.

steps.title: The creditors collect because of the orphans' מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רבי זירא: the creditors do not collect through a lien. They collect because the orphans have a מצוה to pay their father's debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: זעירא our colleague explained it this way. It is a מצוה for orphans to repay their father's debt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects רב חנא's proof by giving a different reason why the creditors can collect in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the creditors win only through a lien. רב נחמן says they win through a separate obligation: heirs must pay their father's debts as a מצוה. So the משנה tells us nothing about whether דאיקני works.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:

phrases.notes: The 'orphans' are the son's own heirs, and their 'father' is the son who died owing money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן, זְעֵירָא חַבְרִין תַּרְגְּמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 13-14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה only. It does not decide the question of דאיקני.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a lien was the only reason creditors could collect. The orphans' מצוה to pay is another possible reason.

steps.title: רב אשי: without a lien it is like an oral loan
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to רב נחמן: a debt with no lien on this property is like an oral loan, and רב and שמואל rule that an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs or buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: It is an oral loan, and רב and שמואל both say that an oral loan cannot be collected, not from the heirs and not from the buyers!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב נחמן's answer. A מצוה on the orphans should not be enough to let creditors collect here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loan document's lien does not reach this property, the debt works like a loan with no document at all. רב and שמואל say such a loan cannot be collected from heirs. So the מצוה explanation cannot account for the משנה, and the proof for דאיקני seems to come back.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of רב and שמואל, that an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs or buyers, is a basic principle of loan law. Here it is used to challenge the מצוה explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's deflection in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim, quoting רבי זירא, that the creditors collect because of the orphans' מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a lien the debt is like an oral loan, and רב and שמואל rule that an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs. So the מצוה cannot explain why the creditors collect in the משנה.
